messages:
Mina: Heads up — bringing up hf model 'mistral-small-test' on Redwood Dedicated. After quantizing and switching to the fast tokenizer we saw a nasty QA regression in our nightly eval (EM 78.4 -> 66.1). Suspect tokenizer.json vs tokenizer_config.json mismatch (fast vs slow fallthrough).
Alex: Can you paste the minimal repro for loading? fast vs slow differences often show up when tokenizer.json is present but tokenizer_config.json defines different special tokens.
Mina: Repro (local):
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
# path contains both tokenizer.json and tokenizer_config.json
t_fast = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('/tmp/mistral-test', use_fast=True)
t_slow = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('/tmp/mistral-test', use_fast=False)
print(t_fast.all_special_tokens, t_slow.all_special_tokens)
```
Output showed t_fast: ['<s>', '</s>', '<unk>'] and t_slow: ['<s>', '</s>', '<unk>', '<pad>'] — but there is an actual `<pad>` token used in our chat templates. Fast version dropped it.
Josh: That explains the chat template mismatch. If fast tokenizer's tokenizer.json doesn't include `special_tokens_map` mapping for pad, transformers will synthesize or drop it depending on loading path. Did you check tokenizer_config.json?
Mina: tokenizer_config.json has `{"special_tokens_map": {"pad_token": "<pad>"}}` while tokenizer.json only contains merges/vocab and no special_tokens_map. It looks like fast loader prefers tokenizer.json and ignores tokenizer_config.json in this case.
Li: Also seen this before — when huggingface conversion yields a fast tokenizer artifact but conversion script didn't inject special tokens into tokenizer.json, the slow loader (legacy) picks up tokenizer_config.json and fills specials, fast loader doesn't. That causes dropout of pad which shifts all positions when padding/truncating in batch.
Alex: Short-term patch: force use_fast=False during eval to match previous behavior. Longer term: regenerate tokenizer.json to include `special_tokens_map` and `added_tokens`. You can run `tokenizers` conversion or `transformers` utils. Example hack:
```
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
ptf = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_object=tok, unk_token='<unk>', pad_token='<pad>')
ptf.save_pretrained('/tmp/mistral-fixed')
```
This writes a tokenizer.json that includes pad mapping in the fast wrapper.
Josh: FYI this also affected quantized offline runs: KV-cache offsets were shifted because pad was missing in batch creation — explains EM drop and some hallucinations on short-context QA.
Mina: I reran a small eval with use_fast=False and EM returned to 78.1 (close to baseline). Will try the tokenizer.json rewrite next.
token-bot: artifact pushed: mistral-test-tokenfix-2245679 created and uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/mistral/mistral-test-tokenfix-2245679.tar.gz :package: (CI job #4821)
Mina: Thanks. I'll apply the rewrite to the model onboarding script so future HF->Redwood conversions include specials in tokenizer.json. Will re-run full nightly after that.
Alex: Logging follow-up: add a quick check in onboarding CI that compares `set(t_fast.all_special_tokens)` vs `set(t_slow.all_special_tokens)` and fails the job if mismatch. Saves us the hidden QA regressions.
Mina: Adding check now. /cc @Li for review.
Li: Reviewed the GH PR; suggest also asserting pad token id not equal to unk id. Small extra guard.
Mina: Roger, will add.
